## After the workshop {#after-the-course .smaller}

::: {.small}
- **Yours now**: a reproduced result, an estimand statement and a causal graph for a published claim, a declared analysis placed among the `r nrow(spec_curve)` specifications of its curve, and a report whose history shows the declaration before the result
- **Where to go next**: the page [Outside the workshop](../tracks/long/after.html) leads into the companion curriculum, from meta-analysis and the building of the analysis file to scale construction, weights, causal graphs, and the multiverse and its critics
- **The record of the claim**: the SCORE dossier of the paper at osf.io/h7432, the maintained fork of the reanalysis behind the country-year panel at osf.io/6zqct, and the archival record of the robustness study at osf.io/8rtwe
- **Keep going locally**: the research-software and open-research teams at your university, or a ReproducibiliTea journal club near you
:::

::: {.fragment .none}
Everything on the workshop's website is open, and you can fork any of it.
:::

::: notes
That is the end of the workshop. Three days ago we started from what a claim in social science is for and why its credibility became a question. Since then you have reproduced a recorded result to the third decimal, said precisely which question the claim answers, declared an analysis before running it, placed it among every justifiable alternative, learnt the methods behind those alternatives at the level of the country-year and of the respondent, and written it up in a report whose history anyone can check. The page Outside the workshop leads into the modules that three days could only touch, and the OSF holds the record of the claim, from the SCORE dossier to the archive of the robustness study. For company in keeping these habits, most universities have research-software and open-research teams, and ReproducibiliTea journal clubs meet in many places. [advance] Everything on the workshop's website is open, and you can take any of it and make it your own.
:::
